title: Debiased Negative Mining Improves Out-of-distribution Detection with Pre-trained Vision-Language Models

problem.claim: The paper addresses mining true negative labels for post-hoc OOD scoring with pre-trained vision-language models.

gap.claim: Existing heuristic approaches for mining negative labels from unlabeled wild data do not adequately address false negatives.

contributions.claim: A theoretical framework is developed to correct sampling bias in negative labels by indirectly approximating their distribution.
Debiased negative mining is converted into Monte Carlo sampling using ID labels and unlabeled wild-corpus data.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments establish a new state-of-the-art across various OOD detection setups.

narrative_sequence.summary: OOD detection is presented as a way to improve machine-learning reliability by identifying inputs from unknown classes.
The work studies post-hoc OOD detection with pre-trained VLMs using affinities between ID and negative labels.
Heuristic negative-label mining from unlabeled wild data leaves the false-negative problem insufficiently addressed.
The paper proposes bias correction through an approximated negative-label distribution and Monte Carlo sampling.
Extensive experiments are reported to produce state-of-the-art results across multiple OOD detection setups.

source_observation.claim: Negative labels mined from unlabeled wild data can contain false negatives and introduce sampling bias.

interpretation.claim: When proxy negatives are noisy, modeling or correcting their distribution may improve downstream detection.

application.claim: Use distribution-aware debiasing and sampling when constructing negative examples for OOD scoring.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach transfers beyond the described VLM-based OOD setting.

unknowns: Datasets, baselines, and quantitative experimental results are not specified.
The theoretical assumptions and derivation are not provided.
Implementation details and computational costs are not provided.
